executiveSummary: GM0327's official 2025 identity, centre, 31,911 residents, 28 neighbourhoods, six districts, three BAG places, eleven BRT settlement labels, five road-border records, absence of a ProRail station and 41 scheduled-transit stop areas are coherent. Neighbourhood rows total 31,905 residents, six below the municipality control (-0.019%), which the allocator reconciles without changing the published rows. All ten presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services with finite bounds, exact local reconciliation, causal-ledger closure, layer invariance and monotone event-attributable burden. Release is nevertheless correction-required. A Grebbedijk/Nederrijn failure is a real high-consequence mechanism for dike-ring area 45, but the generic river preset selects no water level, dike segment/state, breach, LIWO footprint, probability band, arrival or recession; it assigns a municipality-centre flood-stress field of 0.969793 from T+12 through T+72, 9,258 affected resident-equivalents and 754,146.635 deprived person-hours. Eight active T+24 hazard families reuse the same neighbourhood order, rather than Leusden's distinct Gelderse-Vallei water pathways, urban rain/sewer/groundwater conditions, older-population heat vulnerability, or Utrechtse-Heuvelrug forest/heath and smoke geography. The canonical wildfire has zero local flame and only remote smoke/drought forcing despite official combustible-nature eligibility; a locally sourced fire remains unmodelled. Five road records collapse to three physical corridors and do not encode event-valid passability, bus operation, external acute-care access or village isolation. Public water, electricity-planning, antenna, school and care registers are useful context but do not reveal operational utility topology, backup, live state, staffing, stocks or restoration. Leusden's current public 72-hour preparedness page says emergency-support-point locations are still being investigated, so they must remain Unknown. NoData, no local sensor and no selected event must never be rendered as zero or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0327 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated CBS/BAG/BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; full CBS feature retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK source identifies GM0327 as Leusden and reports 31,911 residents, density 545/km², 24.3% aged 65 or older and 4,538 one-person households in the generated municipality control.

The generated centre [5.411647854460252,52.124134338262756] lies inside the 2025 boundary. The overview MultiPolygon contains 112 coordinate positions; the fresh non-generalized CBS feature contains 2,813, so the overview is selection/display geometry rather than a hydraulic or asset mask.

Twenty-eight neighbourhood rows in six districts sum to 31,905 residents (-6, -0.019%), 13,985 households and 7,725 independently rounded residents aged 65-plus. All core rows are retained and allocated back to the 31,911 municipality control rather than silently rewritten.

BAG supplies Leusden, Stoutenburg and Achterveld and BRT supplies eleven labels: four woonkernen, one deelkern and six buurtschappen. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and BRT is CC BY 4.0; settlement population labels and municipal statistics are distinct source products.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Omgevingsvisie, water-and-sewer programme start note and dated sewer evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Omgevingsvisie adopted 2023; programme start note published 17 September 2025; GRP 2019–2023 extended through 31 December 2025; pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The adopted vision describes Leusden as relatively low and wet: Gelderse-Vallei brooks drain through the Valleikanaal and Eem, Heuvelrug infiltration returns as seepage, and low areas east/north of the Valleikanaal including Laapeerseweg and Modderbeek are waterlogging-sensitive. This is static system/context evidence, not a live flood footprint.

The current programme start note identifies groundwater-protection areas north-east and south of the Leusden core, consequence reduction for a large floodable area and designated water-storage areas east/north of the Valleikanaal. It covers wastewater, rainwater and groundwater duties but exposes no machine-readable catchment, live sewer/pump state, capacity or restoration feed.

The dated GRP records more than 50 mm in one hour on 28 July 2014 and water nuisance in Achterveld, while explicitly saying sewer capacity remains limited and some street water is unavoidable in extreme rainfall. That historical observation and policy ambition must not be projected as a current observation or forecast.

A 2024 Tabaksteeg-Zuid development document identifies high to very high wet-weather groundwater, seepage, pressure sewerage, an older mixed sewer in Leusden-Zuid and reported cellar water. These are site/planning findings, not municipality-wide current pump or groundwater state; no standard redistribution licence or update cadence is stated for the municipal PDFs.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe / Gemeente Leusden / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Current drought context, local water mechanisms and public water-asset registers
evidenceSources.edition: Water picture updated 2 September 2026; Leusden withdrawal notice dated 11 June 2026 and effective 12 June 2026; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: The water board's timestamped 2 September 2026 regional picture says drought has not ended and groundwater remains well below normal; spatial rainfall was uneven. It is regional current context with update/valid time, not a Leusden point value or automatic synthetic-scenario forcing.

Leusden's official notice records an indefinite surface-water withdrawal ban from 12 June 2026 for the Valleikanaal, Heiligenbergerbeek and all ditches, subject to continuing water-board monitoring. This is a dated operational measure, not proof of future T+0 conditions or drinking-water outage.

The partial public HWH assignment contains 80 objects in GM0327: 73 weirs, five surface-water pumps and two sewer pumps, including named Leusden-centre and Achterveld sewer pumps. IMWA Kunstwerken is national/weekly and Waterketen DAMO contributor-dependent; both are CC BY-SA 4.0.

Asset points, 'realised' register status and sometimes-null numeric capacity fields do not establish connectivity, compatible units, control rules, power dependency, telemetry, current operation, backup, crew access or restoration. Missing objects and null attributes remain NoData/Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023, Crisisplan 2024–2027 and nature-fire readiness context
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile 2023; crisis plan 2024–2027; public nature-fire phase page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: VRU treats river flooding as catastrophic and separately identifies extreme rain, storm, heat/drought, nature fire, vital-infrastructure loss and cyber dependence. Electricity loss can cascade to road, water and rail transport, while cyber incidents can disrupt energy, drinking-water and water systems.

The profile states that a major Utrechtse-Heuvelrug nature fire can require several days of intensive response and weeks of crisis and medical capacity; it highlights more than 150 care locations region-wide, difficult timely evacuation and recreation/access constraints. Those are regional planning figures, not Leusden incident occupancy or resource availability.

The current VRU page reported nature-fire risk Phase 1 at access time and warns that mobile reach is not universal, escape should be across the wind toward a road/hard surface/built-up area, and access routes must remain clear. Phase 1 is a timestamped regional readiness class, not zero ignition probability or a forecast through T+72.

The crisis plan distinguishes acute flash crises, forecast/scalable events and prolonged project-like crises. The public documents provide dated governance context with no machine incident cadence, local dispatch/evacuation decision, resource ledger or standard redistribution licence stated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Watermanagementcentrum Nederland / Rijkswaterstaat / Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe
evidenceSources.title: E05 — LIWO interpretation and Grebbedijk/Gelderse-Vallei water-safety mechanism
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO public documentation inspected 3 September 2026; Grebbedijk water-board context current at access; Waterinfo snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: LIWO contains professional flood-preparedness layers whose correct interpretation requires water-manager expertise. A scenario must retain release, defence/breach case, probability band, depth/arrival/recession surface, resolution, units, coverage, NoData and licence rather than convert centre distance into an observed local depth.

The Grebbedijk between Wageningen and Rhenen protects the Gelderse Vallei against Nederrijn high water. Municipal risk evidence for dike-ring area 45 says a southern breach can have large effects in Leusden; the north-side Eem/rand-lake mechanism is materially different. This supports a selected breach scenario, not the simulator's unlabelled municipality-wide scalar.

The public deployment snapshot contains no Waterinfo observation or forecast point assigned inside GM0327. Amerongen-boven is 16.55 km from the municipality reference point and observed 613 cm NAP at 17:30Z on 2 September 2026; that point value is neither Grebbedijk condition nor Leusden inundation.

Waterinfo is generally CC0, commonly ten-minute observation context and a public non-mission-critical service; forecast coverage declines by horizon and the retrieved national endpoint returns no T+72 water-level features. Absence is NoData, never zero water or no flood hazard.

evidenceSources.publisher: IPO Risicokaart / Provincie Utrecht / Veiligheidsregio Utrecht
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Utrechtse-Heuvelrug combustible-nature and forest/heath exposure context
evidenceSources.edition: Risicokaart metadata updated 19 February 2026; two Utrechtse-Heuvelrug features valid from 16 May 2024; provincial nature description published 2023
supports: A bounded WFS query returns two province-Utrecht features named Utrechtse Heuvelrug relevant to Leusden: a broad mixed-forest-with-heath area and a smaller mixed deciduous/coniferous woodland polygon at the municipality's southern side. A third bbox hit is Barneveld-sourced and demonstrates why bbox hits cannot be treated as municipal containment.

The provincial description identifies the connected Den Treek and Leusderheide landscape, including dry heath, drift sand and forest. VRU says warmer and longer dry periods make a large nature fire exceeding normal response capacity realistic in the region.

The Risicokaart nature-fire layer is Public Domain static eligibility/context, with feature-validity dates but no promised operational cadence, fire-risk score or population. It is not ignition, live fuel/moisture, incident perimeter, spread, smoke, access or suppression.

Canonical wildfire at T+24 has zero local flame, smoke 0.472917 and drought 0.646465. A remote smoke exercise may legitimately have no local flame, but it does not test a Den-Treek/Leusderheide ignition, evacuation or firewater/access problem.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Road, scheduled-transit and external acute-care access context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail and GTFS deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; NDW publication 2 September 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB graph has five mobility/supply-only border records: A28 to Amersfoort, N226 to Amersfoort and Woudenberg, and N227 to Amersfoort and Woudenberg. The paired N226 and N227 records share physical-corridor IDs; their nominal 150-unit values are series/boundary proxies and non-additive, while A28 carries 260 scenario units.

No CC0 ProRail station lies inside GM0327. OVapi GTFS version 9543, retrieved 31 August and valid 30 August–12 December 2026 under free-use/best-effort/no-SLA terms, yields 41 in-boundary stop areas; schedules and geometry do not establish live bus service, passenger count, accessibility, vehicle capacity or disaster operation.

Two NDW records within about 1.82 and 2.49 km of the reference point were real vehicle obstructions with unknown severity at the 2 September snapshot. Point proximity does not identify A28/N226/N227 passability, and no matching record is not evidence that a road is open.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 has no point in GM0327. Meander Medisch Centrum in Amersfoort is nearest at 5.93 km straight-line and reports a 24/7 emergency department, seventeen rooms and 34,161 visits in 2025; questionnaire context is not travel time, diversion, staffing, occupancy or guaranteed receiving capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Leusden / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / KNMI / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — 72-hour preparedness, electricity planning, communications, schools and monitoring gaps
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal pages inspected 3 September 2026; public deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: Leusden instructs households to prepare for three days with water, food, medicines, radio, power bank and a personal/neighbour plan. It says the municipality and VRU are still investigating emergency-support-point locations and will publish them once known; therefore no location or capacity is currently validated.

The current municipal net-congestion page says capacity in the Amersfoort region is very limited, although the wider Utrecht connection stop does not apply there. One NBNL postcode sample at 3832JN maps to Stedin area TS049_10 Leusden and reports 4.7 MW/20-request withdrawal and 2 MW/8-request injection queues, 28 projects and earliest year 2029, while existing/required capacities are null. NBNL is at-least-quarterly/monthly planning context with no exact standard licence identifier found, not live load, outage or reserve.

RDI assigns 48 antenna installations: 22 mobile, four fixed-link and 22 amateur; its public service states no standard reuse licence or cadence. Daily attribution-licensed DUO assigns 29 education locations: eleven primary, one secondary and seventeen other registered. Registers do not establish coverage, backhaul, backup, occupancy, shelter role, capacity or operation.

No KNMI station, RIVM PM2.5 point or 365-day KNMI seismic origin lies inside GM0327. De Bilt weather is nearest at 16.09 km, Utrecht-Griftpark PM2.5 at 19.52 km and an induced M1.72 Noordbeemster origin at 58.69 km. KNMI observations/seismic are CC BY 4.0; current RIVM air data are indicative hourly observations with no standard reuse licence stated. No-match is not zero local weather, air exposure or seismic hazard.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0327 pnpm audit:model passed two tests covering severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
Focused inline Vite runs captured all presets at T+24 and T+72 and the complete river/compound trajectories without creating a repository test file.

Coastal T+24 has zero direct inundation and only wind-related residual pressure; earthquake has zero selected ground motion; canonical wildfire has zero local flame and remote smoke/drought. These are scenario states, not claims that local coastal-supply, seismic or fire risk is absent.
Outputs are deterministic exercise indices and resident-equivalents, not observations, probabilities, casualties, measured flood depth or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation, ledger closure and cumulative burden pass.
notes: All service availability remains in [0,1]; hazard fields, demand, delivery, affected residents and deprived person-hours remain finite and non-negative.
Zero-intensity scenarios return exact zero event hazard, affected population and event-attributable burden; repeated runs are deterministic and cumulative burden is monotone.
Every service allocates all 28 neighbourhoods and reconciles to 31,911 residents; local demand and delivery close to municipality totals and selected layer does not mutate the hazard scenario.
Arithmetic validity does not establish local hydraulic, fire, utility, route, facility, occupancy or recovery validity.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The unselected river scalar and common neighbourhood seed do not represent Leusden's distinct flood, rain, heat, fire and cyber geographies.
notes: River internal flood stress rises from zero at T+0 to 0.341367 at T+6 and 0.969793 at T+12, then remains exactly unchanged through T+72 without a selected Grebbedijk state/breach, Nederrijn hydrograph, LIWO footprint, probability, arrival or recession.

At T+24 severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Rozendaal, Bosveld, Rossenberg, Hamersveld-Oud, 't Ruige Veld, Stoutenburg and Hamershof in the same order; compound merely swaps the first two.

Official evidence instead distinguishes low/wet Valleikanaal and brook areas, Achterveld rain nuisance, high wet-weather groundwater/seepage near Leusden-Zuid, older-resident heat need and southern forest/heath eligibility. One shared order cannot validate all mechanisms.

Administrative centres and a scenario seed are not substitutes for dike/breach cells, elevation/catchment, rain-sewer surface, groundwater, shade/demography, ignition/perimeter, smoke plume or cyber source/target.

serviceDependencies.summary: Road-only transfer is correctly separated from utilities, but all exact local lifeline dependencies remain synthetic or absent.
notes: The five NWB records affect only mobility and road-logistics supply and are explicitly logical proxies, avoiding false electricity/gas/water equivalence; they still lack current passability, direction, measured emergency capacity and destination state.

Eighty water assets are not a connected brook/surface-water/sewer/pump graph and do not alter drainage or water recovery. Electricity planning and provider context do not establish physical power/gas topology or outage/restoration.

RDI antennas do not establish coverage/backhaul/power; GTFS does not establish bus operation; DUO locations and an external emergency department do not establish shelter/care operation, backup, staff or capacity.
Exact T+24/T+72 availability values across eight services remain transparent synthetic indices until safe aggregate operator, municipality, water-board, transit and care evidence is supplied.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical cause ledgers close, but source selection, evidence validity and accountable first-72-hour decisions remain outside the graph.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service contributions reconstruct availability and municipality pressure contributions reconcile exactly.

Public layers correctly remain non-causal context, but trace does not select a dike/breach/footprint, rainfall raster, water/sewer state, ignition/plume, warning, route/bus status, care state or utility outage.

T+0–6 needs event and evidence selection, forecast/warning validation, coordination activation and route/defence/fire surveillance; T+6–24 needs evacuation-versus-shelter, closure, assisted-resident/care decisions and public information.

T+24–48 needs verified outage/water/air/care/logistics status and distribution/support decisions; T+48–72 needs inspection, dewatering/repair milestones, re-entry and unresolved-needs review. Current actions lack owner, trigger, request, decision, resource, execution, verification and rollback states.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent flood disruption is conservative, but exact river and compound plateaus through 72 hours are not locally calibrated or action-linked.
notes: River at T+24 and T+72 retains exactly 0.969793 internal flood stress, 0.300776 severity, 0.345941 pressure, 9,258 affected and unchanged eight-service availability; cumulative burden rises from 186,921.338 to 754,146.635 person-hours.

At river T+72 drainage availability is 0.421888, facilities 0.549270, telecom 0.580709, water 0.600462, power 0.644988, gas 0.781248, supply 0.818809 and mobility 0.824902. These exact values have no local operator evidence.

Compound T+24–72 likewise holds 0.315655 flood stress, approximately 0.486443 pressure, 15,576 affected and nearly all service values fixed, while severity declines and burden reaches 1,085,491.078 person-hours.

Conservative restoration blocking should remain an explicitly synthetic exercise guard. Grebbedijk/Valleikanaal/sewer/fire, routes, care, utilities and support points require evidence-valid milestones before the UI can imply local restoration or re-entry.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, geography, places and demographic controls reconcile.
findings.evidence: GM0327/Leusden/Utrecht/VRU agree; the centre and all BAG place centres are contained. The 31,905 neighbourhood total differs by only -6 (-0.019%) from the 31,911 control.
findings.action: Retain editions, licences, source observations, null/suppression semantics and published-versus-allocated reconciliation; do not rewrite rows or infer incident-time occupancy.

findings.summary: The river preset represents a plausible dike-ring-45 threat with an unselected, false-precision municipality-centre scalar.
findings.evidence: A Grebbedijk/Nederrijn failure can affect Leusden, but no hydrograph, defence state, breach or LIWO cell is selected. Internal flood stress becomes exactly 0.969793 at T+12, stays identical through T+72 and reports 9,258 affected and 754,146.635 person-hours.
findings.action: Suppress this local operational impact unless a versioned authority scenario selects the Grebbedijk/dike section, water boundary, breach/no-breach case, connected footprint, probability band, arrival and recession; preserve Unknown rather than declaring safe.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active hazards reuse one exact neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire at T+24 rank Rozendaal, Bosveld, Rossenberg, Hamersveld-Oud, 't Ruige Veld, Stoutenburg and Hamershof identically, contrary to mechanism-specific official water, groundwater, demographic and nature geography.
findings.action: Replace the common rank seed with source-specific zonal surfaces and event source/target geometry; validate named low/wet, rain-nuisance, heat-vulnerability and combustible-nature contrasts independently.

findings.summary: Pluvial and groundwater effects do not consume Leusden's documented catchment, sewer, seepage and storage mechanisms.
findings.evidence: Municipal evidence distinguishes Valleikanaal/brooks, Laapeerseweg/Modderbeek, Achterveld historical nuisance, Leusden-Zuid mixed/pressure sewer and high wet-weather groundwater; HWH supplies 80 partial asset points. The generic pluvial T+24 field instead reports 0.305299 stress, 2,376 affected and the shared rank.
findings.action: Ingest versioned event rainfall, elevation/imperviousness, municipal stress-test surface and authorized sewer/surface-water/groundwater catchments; keep asset connectivity/state Unknown where unavailable.

findings.summary: Official Utrechtse-Heuvelrug eligibility is not connected to a selected ignition, flame, smoke, access or evacuation model.
findings.evidence: Risicokaart/Province/VRU establish mixed forest, heath and prolonged response/evacuation risk around Den Treek/Leusderheide. Canonical T+24 wildfire has local flame zero, smoke 0.472917, drought 0.646465 and 667 affected, with the common rank and no source/plume.
findings.action: Keep the canonical case clearly labelled remote-smoke-only; add a separate locally sourced exercise requiring ignition/perimeter, land cover/fuel/moisture, event-valid wind, people present, access, firewater and suppression state.

findings.summary: Public infrastructure context cannot validate exact power, water, drainage, gas, telecom and facility availability.
findings.evidence: E03/E08 supply partial asset/register/planning counts but no safe physical topology, live load/state, switching/control, backup, staff, stock, crew or restoration. River T+72 nevertheless publishes eight exact local availability values from 0.421888 to 0.824902.
findings.action: Retain these as scenario estimates, never operator status. Seek safe aggregate service zones, outage/status snapshots, dependency classes, backup bands and restoration ranges; leave unavailable/security-sensitive fields Unknown.

findings.summary: Road, bus, rural-village and external-care continuity are not causally tested through 72 hours.
findings.evidence: Five NWB records collapse to A28/N226/N227 and only serve mobility/supply proxies; there is no local rail station, GTFS provides 41 scheduled stops, and the nearest public acute-care point is Meander 5.93 km away. None carries event-valid passability or capacity.
findings.action: Deduplicate physical corridors, intersect selected hazard cells with direction/segment/bridge state, consume valid-time NDW/transit status when available and model external care/supply destinations with Unknown capacity and explicit alternatives.

findings.summary: River and compound service states plateau exactly from T+24 through T+72 without locally evidenced milestones.
findings.evidence: River retains identical stress, pressure, affected count and service vector after T+24; compound retains 15,576 affected and near-identical service values while burden reaches 1,085,491.078 person-hours. No local defence, dewatering, road, care or operator milestone supports the precision.
findings.action: Retain conservative repair blocking as a synthetic guard but attach uncertainty and action/evidence gates; update only on verified water recession, inspection, route access, facility acceptance and operator restoration milestones.

findings.summary: The first-72-hour interface has impacts but no accountable action-state machine.
findings.evidence: VRU distinguishes acute, forecast and prolonged crises, and Leusden asks households to prepare for 72 hours while emergency-support points remain under investigation. The model does not trace warning/selection, evacuation/shelter, vulnerable outreach, route closure, care transfer, distribution, inspection, re-entry or unresolved need.
findings.action: Add scenario-specific T+0–6, 6–24, 24–48 and 48–72 action records with owner, trigger, source validity, request/decision, resources, dependencies, execution, verification, expiry and rollback; do not fabricate support-point locations.

findings.summary: Observation/register gaps can be misread as zero or all-clear without strict provenance semantics.
findings.evidence: There is no local Waterinfo, KNMI weather, RIVM PM2.5, acute-care or seismic point; NBNL existing/required capacity is null; HWH capacities are partly null; Phase 1 fire risk and 48-hour warning horizons are time-bounded. Nearby points and no-match categories do not fill those gaps.
findings.action: Expose publisher, product/version, retrieval and issue/valid time, spatial coverage/resolution, evidence class, unit/datum, quality, cadence, licence and explicit Unknown/NoData/stale state on every layer; never coerce missing to zero/safe.

findings.summary: Coastal and earthquake direct impacts are appropriately zero in the canonical cases but do not exhaust indirect or alternate local risk.
findings.evidence: Coastal direct inundation and earthquake ground motion are zero at T+24; no 365-day event origin lies inside GM0327. Coastal/wind and supply dependencies, natural seismic hazard and future events remain outside those bounded selected cases.
findings.action: Retain exact zero only as a selected-scenario result with the source/footprint visible; keep unselected indirect disruption and absent observations Unknown, and do not claim municipality safety.

corrections.summary: Replace municipality-centre flood forcing and the common neighbourhood seed with governed source-specific hazard adapters.
corrections.validation: For river flooding, use LIWO/WMCN versioned professional scenario layers and a water-board-selected Grebbedijk/dike-ring-45 event, preserving dike/breach case, probability band, boundary condition, issue/valid time, units/datum, cell/resolution, coverage, NoData and licence; LIWO interpretation requires water-manager review and is not live telemetry. For pluvial/groundwater, use authorized municipality/Vallei en Veluwe stress-test and catchment products plus AHN/land-cover only with per-product date, resolution and licence. Suppress local operational impacts when event selection is absent; validate source containment, arrival/recession and independent neighbourhood ranks.

residualLimitations: The audit verifies a deterministic planning simulator, not an operational prediction, evacuation order, casualty model, hydraulic computation, wildfire forecast or utility restoration promise.

CBS controls and neighbourhood values are annual rounded/suppressed resident statistics; they do not represent incident-time occupancy, visitors, workers, pupils, patients, carers, responders or displaced people.
The full CBS boundary is administrative. Grebbedijk compartments, Valleikanaal/brook catchments, sewers, groundwater, forest fuel, smoke, roads and service areas require their own physical geometry.
LIWO and water-board context establish plausible scenario families but not a selected current breach, defence state, probability, inundation, arrival, recession, evacuation or re-entry decision.
HWH coverage is contributor-dependent; points and numeric fields do not establish connected topology, units, live state, power dependency, backup, access or restoration.

NWB/NDW, ProRail/GTFS, NBNL, RDI, DUO and RIVM have different coverage and time semantics and do not establish live passability, service continuity, occupancy, topology, capacity, staffing, backup or stocks.
Risicokaart combustible nature establishes static eligibility only, not current ignition, fuels/moisture, perimeter, spread, smoke plume, access, people present or suppression.

No local public Waterinfo, KNMI weather, PM2.5, seismic or acute-care point exists in the deployment snapshot; nearest-point values may not be interpolated or treated as local truth without a validated method.
Utility and telecom physical topology can be unavailable or security-sensitive; a minimal transparent synthetic fallback is preferable to invented sensitive precision.
Emergency-support-point locations, capacities and activation rules are Unknown because Leusden states that candidate locations are still being investigated.
